title: Hops infusion for sleeplessness
subtitle: A bedtime tea of Humulus lupulus for difficulty falling asleep
excerpt: Hops infusion is a bedtime tea of dried Humulus lupulus strobiles steeped for 10 minutes and drunk 30 to 45 minutes before sleep. A sedative nervine with a well-established traditional use in European herbal practice for difficulty falling asleep and nervous restlessness at bedtime. The bitter sedative compounds in hops, methylbutenol and lupuline, work gently and without residual drowsiness. Strongly bitter flavour, best combined with a little honey.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), hops entry, Botanical.com. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Humulus lupulus L., strobilus (2014, EMA/HMPC/418902/2005 Rev. 1), open access.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried hops stores 6 months in a sealed tin, they degrade faster than most herbs. Brew each cup fresh.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb that acts on the nervous system to reduce nervous excitability, promote relaxation, and support sleep. A sedative nervine differs from a relaxant nervine in having a stronger and more direct sleep-promoting action. Hops is one of the most reliably sedative herbs in European practice.

content.text: Hops infusion is a bedtime tea of dried hop strobiles, steeped under cover for 10 minutes and drunk 30 to 45 minutes before sleep. A

with a long European tradition for difficulty falling asleep and the restless, racing-mind pattern of bedtime anxiety. A compound produced from hops' bitter acids is directly sedative. The flavour is intensely bitter, one of the most bitter of the common herbal teas, and is best taken with a small spoon of honey.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Place 1 tablespoon of dried hops cones in a teapot or heatproof cup. Pour 200 ml of just-boiled water over the herb. Cover and steep for 10 minutes.
Strain into a cup. Add honey to taste, the bitterness is significant and honey makes the infusion more palatable.
Drink 30 to 45 minutes before the intended sleep time.

One cup at bedtime, taken as needed. For persistent difficulty sleeping, one cup nightly for up to 4 weeks then reassess. Hops works best in combination with good sleep habits, consistent bedtime, reduced screen light, cool room.
Dried hops strobiles degrade faster than most herbs, store in a sealed tin for up to 6 months. Use fresh stock. old hops loses its sedative potency quickly.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use alongside alcohol, sedative medication, or if you are being treated for depression. See a doctor for insomnia lasting more than 4 weeks. Also see a doctor for poor sleep that comes with low mood, fatigue, weight change, or other unexplained symptoms.
